title: fr blend
parentNote: Today is fr at the front of a word — frog, frost, frill. It is the near twin of yesterday's fl, and that is on purpose: same f, different second sound, so "flag" and "frog" start almost alike and a child has to listen past the first letter. The r is where it goes wrong, because r needs the lips to round and the tongue to pull back, and it is easy to skip — "frog" comes out "fog", "frill" comes out "fill". Say the pair on its own a few times, ffff-r, and watch that their lips move. If they read "fuh-rog", the f is too long; clip it and let the two sounds touch.

activities.mouthCue: Top teeth on your bottom lip for the f, then round your lips and pull your tongue back for the r.
activities.prompt: This pair is not like sh or ch. Here you really do hear both letters — they are just in a hurry.
These two both start with f. Find the one that ends with a growl, not a hum.
Two of these are half of the third. Find the one that is both.
The new blend goes first. Slide the two sounds together before you say the rest.
Only the middle has changed. Keep the front exactly the same.
A frock is a dress. The ck at the back is one quick pop.
Sound out frog, then add the ending on: frog — s.
The longest one. A blend at the front and a blend at the back.
One of these has an extra sound at the front. Listen before the vowel.
Same again. Is the growl in there or not?
All three start the same way. This time the clue is at the end.

activities.text: Is the frog on a flat rock?
The frost is on the grass and it is thick.
That frog is fat and it can swim fast.

activities.title: The frog and the frost
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: The frost is thick and the pond is stiff.
A fat frog did hop on and did land flat.
The frog did kick and did slip and did not swim.
Pam did lift it off and sat it on a soft rag.
The frog did hop back on and did slip off in a flash!

questions.prompt: The frog did land flat on it.
Pam sat the frog on it.
